activities.anchor: you have met all of them
activities.caption: pair each strengthening move with its mechanism
activities.name: mcpStrengthenMatch

config.prompt: The metallurgist's menu — pair each move with the mechanism and the tell-tale example:

pairs.right: odd-sized solute atoms pin the lattice — tin in copper, bronze, c. 3300 bce
deformation multiplies dislocations until they jam each other — the hammered edge
Hall–Petch: boundaries block slip — microalloyed pipeline steels
dissolve, quench, hold warm so fine obstacles nucleate — Wilm's duralumin, 1906

config.why: Every entry is a way of adding obstacles to dislocation motion: a metal's strength is its obstacles, not its packing.

activities.anchor: Every knife, spring, rail and bearing
activities.caption: rebuild the quench-and-temper sequence
activities.name: mcpQuenchOrder

config.prompt: From soft iron to a tough blade — drag the heat-treatment story into order:
items: Heat the steel hot: iron switches structure and dissolves its carbon
Quench: the carbon is trapped in a distorted structure — martensite
Temper: reheat moderately so some carbon precipitates out
Result: a little hardness traded for a lot of toughness
config.why: Ancient smiths reverse-engineered the whole map empirically; metallurgy later supplied the coordinates.

activities.anchor: ceramics made several times tougher by engineering their own flaw response
activities.caption: walk the taming-a-ceramic decision
activities.name: mcpTameBranch

config.root: A ceramic part has to survive service. Walk the design questions.

start.text: What will attack the part first?

choices.label: Bending will put one face in tension
choices.feedback: Then never let the material feel it.

choices.label: It begins life as a powder

prestress.text: Pull the steel bars, cast around them, release: the ceramic is permanently squeezed, so ordinary loads never produce net tension.

sinter.text: Press and sinter: diffusion bonds the particles below melting — the vacancy machinery of the last lesson doing factory work.

toughen.text: Transformation toughening: a metastable phase transforms at a crack tip and expands about 4% by volume, squeezing the crack shut — toughness multiplied by the material's own response.

config.why: Keep tension out, squeeze cracks shut, build without melting — the tricks that tame a locked-bond family.

activities.caption: one line of the hardness note mislabels brittleness
activities.name: mcpBrittleSpot

config.prompt: A note comparing failure modes — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: Concrete's tensile strength is poor — a few megapascals.
Its compressive strength runs to tens of megapascals.
Brittle materials are always the weak ones.
Technical ceramics hold hardness and melting points no metal approaches.
Brittleness is a flaw problem: the largest crack in the part calls the shots.
config.correction: Brittle does not mean weak: the ceiling can be very high while the failure mode stays unforgiving — strength is set by the biggest flaw the part carries (Weibull statistics).
config.why: Brittleness names a failure personality — unforgiving about tension and flaws — not a low ceiling.

activities.caption: pair each chain dial with its consequence
activities.name: mcpDialMatch

config.prompt: Four structural dials set a polymer's personality — pair dial with consequence:

pairs.right: longer chains entangle more — strength and viscosity climb with molecular weight
branched chains pack poorly and slide — LDPE film, soft and flexible
covalent bridges lock everything into one molecule — a thermoset that softens never

config.why: Linear chains pack into crystalline lamellae — HDPE milk jugs, stiffer and opaque-ish — the same dial read the other way.

activities.caption: call the stretch before you read the number
activities.name: mcpRubberEstimate

config.prompt: Vulcanised rubber stretches and then snaps back. Roughly what percentage of its original length can it stretch?
config.why: About 500% — the sulfur cross-links store the chains' disorder like springs and hand it back on unloading.
config.context: Goodyear, 1839: a sticky mess turned into a material.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the failure mode that rewrote the manuals
activities.name: mcpDelamCloze

config.text: Composites do not dent, they %%0%% — an impact can leave an invisible interior crack, so aircraft laminates are inspected by %%1%%, and design allowables are set by %%2%% impact damage, not just static strength.
config.hint: One word for the failure mode, one for the inspection that hunts it, one for the design phrase.

activities.caption: file each material by its end-of-life profile
activities.name: mcpEndOfLifeBuckets

config.prompt: The environmental ledger — file each entry:

items.label: steel — remelts with almost nothing lost, hundreds of megatonnes a year
aluminium — recycling saves ~95% of smelting energy
polymers — persist for centuries and mostly down-cycle
a 50-metre wind-turbine blade in epoxy — no economic recycling route today

config.why: End-of-life profiles differ as sharply as properties: the family that performs best in service is the hardest one to unmake.
